analysis.investment_thesis: Cohance (formerly Suven Pharma) is experiencing a multi-year earnings deterioration — net profit has nearly halved from 454 Cr in FY22 to 265 Cr in FY25 — while trading at an absurd EV/EBITDA of 94.69x and P/S of 13.86x. The massive balance sheet restructuring (total assets jumped from 2,254 to 5,568 Cr in one year with a name change) introduces corporate strategy uncertainty at the worst possible time.
key_strengths: CDMO business model benefits from global pharma outsourcing tailwind — structural demand driver is real
OCF positive across all 5 years, with 288 Cr operating cash flow in FY25 showing underlying cash-generating ability
Promoter at 57.49% and DII at 21.57% indicate institutional confidence in the long-term transformation thesis
key_risks: Operating income has been contracting for three consecutive years — 582 Cr (FY22) → 375 Cr (FY25), a 36% fall
Operating margin of just 8.89% is dangerously thin for a specialty pharma/CDMO claiming differentiated chemistry capabilities
Borrowings surged from 65 Cr (FY24) to 451 Cr (FY25) — sudden debt accumulation accompanying the balance sheet transformation raises questions
red_flags: EV/EBITDA of 94.69x is indefensible for a business with declining earnings — this is speculation, not investing
Total assets ballooned from 2,254 Cr to 5,568 Cr in a single year alongside a name change — suggests a large acquisition whose strategic merit and integration risk are unclear
Revenue peaked at 1,340 Cr in FY23 and has not recovered to that level — core business momentum is absent
analysis.detailed_analysis:
I have no interest in paying 94x EV/EBITDA for a business whose profits have fallen nearly 42% from peak. Suven Pharma was a good, debt-light CDMO business but the earnings trajectory since FY22 has been consistently downward — revenue, EBITDA, and net profit have all contracted materially. The 8.89% operating margin is alarming for a company supposedly in value-added specialty pharma; good CDMOs should command 25-35% EBITDA margins, not single digits.

The sudden transformation in FY25 — new name (Cohance Lifesciences), total assets nearly tripling to 5,568 Cr, equity jumping by 1,736 Cr, borrowings up 7x — suggests a major acquisition or merger has occurred. While CDMO is a sector I respect, buying into a business undergoing a complete identity change with deteriorating core fundamentals and a 94x EV/EBITDA price tag is not investing — it is paying for hope. I will watch this from the sidelines until the new entity demonstrates 2-3 years of earnings recovery with clear margin improvement.
